rationales.wacc: Judgment, CAPM-based; round 2 adopts the unrounded figure of 10.7% (round 1 used 10.5%). Cost of equity = risk-free rate of about 4.25% + beta of about 1.3 x equity risk premium of 5.0% = 10.75%. Beta, ERP and the risk-free rate are analyst assumptions: the snapshot has no index or rate series, so none can be estimated or sourced here. Beta is above 1 because revenue depends on cyclical hyperscaler and AI-infrastructure capex, and below the roughly 1.7-2.0 of a high-volatility semi because NVDA is a mega-cap. Debt is LongTermDebt $33.366B (F-de060525b4, total debt: short-term 1.000B + long-term 32.366B) against equity market value of about $5.05T (24,100M cover-page shares x $209.66 close on 2026-08-26), so debt weight is about 0.66%. With an assumed after-tax cost of debt of about 3.7% (assumption, no sourced yield), WACC = 0.9934 x 10.75% + 0.0066 x 3.7% = about 10.70%. Why the change: in round 1 we rounded 10.7% down by about 20-25bp to 10.5% and gave no reason. There was no analytical basis for rounding down, and one decimal matches the precision of the inputs, so we now use 0.107 as computed. We did not choose it with the rating in view. Rating sensitivity (offline, code's dcf() and blending formula, other inputs unchanged; the Neutral band starts when the target price rounds to $189 or more, i.e. upside above -10%, against the $209.66 close): with code's current net cash (-10.923B), the rating turns Neutral at WACC of about 10.19% or lower; with marketable debt securities of $34.143B added to net cash, at about 10.29%; with debt securities plus equity securities at a 30% haircut, at about 10.37%; with both lines at full value, at about 10.41%. So the 10.7% base is about 51bp above the Neutral threshold on code's net cash, about 41bp with debt securities included and about 33bp with debt plus haircut equity. A WACC near 10.0-10.2%, which is within the uncertainty of the beta and ERP assumptions, would move the rating to Neutral. At 10.5% (round-1 value) upside is -12.2% (code net cash), -11.3% (with debt securities) and -10.8% (with debt plus haircut equity). The terminal share of EV is 71.1% at 10.7%.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0%: long-run nominal growth roughly in line with global nominal GDP plus a small premium for secular growth in compute demand. That is well below WACC (10.7%) and inside the gate bound of [0, 4%]. We do not use a higher rate because the explicit period already ends with growth fading to 5%, and AI-infrastructure spending carries real cyclical and competitive risk (custom accelerators at AVGO and MRVL, GPUs at AMD).
rationales.revenue_growth: Years 2-5 apply to code's NTM revenue, which comes from assumptions.json: four quarters from FY2027Q3 to FY2028Q2, about $492B; FY2027Q3 is anchored on the $108.0B guide (Q-1). The exit run-rate of FY2028Q2 (about $137B x 4 = about $549B) is already about 11.5% above NTM with no further sequential growth, so year 2 at 15% assumes only modest sequential growth continues. After that, growth fades to 10%, 7% and 5% as the AI build-out matures and competition rises. No China Data Center compute revenue is assumed (Q-2). This is judgment; no guidance exists beyond FY2027Q3.
rationales.fcf_margin: Margins are grounded in history, measured as CFO (NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) minus capex (PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets), relative to Revenues, using the year-to-date XBRL facts. FY2024: (28.090-1.069)/60.922 = 44.4% (F-c6d18e3588, F-9442a91323, F-a650c0b6ab, as re-reported in the FY2026 10-K). FY2025: (64.089-3.236)/130.497 = 46.6% (F-0895726b1c, F-3eba3b27d5, F-053ca36afd). FY2026: (102.718-6.042)/215.938 = 44.8% (F-48ea7477fe, F-b12a70d09b, F-d514650a55). H1 FY2027: (74.421-4.434)/177.837 = 39.4% (F-e325572968, F-2b25fa17c5, F-f21b6e99e6). TTM to 2026-07-26: (102.718-42.779+74.421)-(6.042-3.122+4.434) over (215.938-90.805+177.837) = 127.0/303.0 = 41.9% (H1 FY2026 comparatives F-fb481caf7b, F-38691604f8, F-b869ccf9b6). The H1 FY2027 shortfall comes from working capital. The 10-Q cash flow statement shows accounts receivable -24.6B (from extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements, per MD&A), inventories -10.2B and prepaid/other -6.5B, partly offset by payables and accruals. Commitments rose to $279B, mainly for memory procurement (Q-10). Year 1 is set at 42%, close to TTM, because we assume this drag continues for a while. Years 2-3 are set at 44%, near the three-year full-year average of about 45%, as revenue growth slows and working-capital investment eases. Years 4-5 fade to 43% and 42% for competitive pressure on gross margin, which is 74% guided (Q-3) versus about 75% recently. CFO already adds back stock-based compensation (H1 FY2027 $3.954B, about 2% of revenue), so these margins are before SBC; dilution is reflected only through the share count. CFO also excludes the $23.7B of H1 gains on equity securities that sit in net income, which is why we use CFO-based FCF and not earnings.
rationales.peers: AMD, AVGO and MRVL, all from config/project.yaml coverage. AMD is the direct merchant GPU/accelerator competitor. AVGO (custom AI accelerators/XPUs plus Ethernet data-center networking) and MRVL (custom AI silicon and data-center interconnect) compete for the same hyperscaler AI-infrastructure budgets. Excluded: INTC (CPU/foundry turnaround with negative TTM earnings; not comparable on margins or growth); MU (memory, a commodity price cycle; NVDA is its customer); AMAT, LRCX and KLAC (wafer-fab equipment, a different end market); SNPS and CDNS (EDA software); ALAB, CRDO and MPWR (connectivity and power-component suppliers with TTM revenue of $1-3B, too small and too high-multiple, about 20-42x EV/Sales, to be fair EV/Sales comparators for a company with about $300B of revenue). In a rough offline check using the snapshot, TTM EV/Sales was AMD about 18.9x, AVGO about 23.0x and MRVL about 24.7x, so the median is about 23.0x. NVDA itself trades at about 16.7x on TTM revenue of about $303B. Peer TTM windows end May-June 2026, compared with July 2026 for NVDA. Specifically, code's TTM windows end 2026-06-27 for AMD, 2026-05-03 for AVGO and 2026-05-02 for MRVL, compared with 2026-07-26 for NVDA, so the peer windows lag NVDA by about one to three months. Given fast AI-related growth at all three, a lagged TTM revenue denominator tends to overstate peer EV/Sales slightly relative to a window aligned with NVDA's; we accept this because each peer's latest filed quarter at the cutoff is used and no aligned data exist. Separately, the 'calendar' field in computed peers.json labels every peer 'CY2025Q4'. That label comes from code (xbrl.calendar_label, which takes the midpoint of the four-quarter TTM window), not from these inputs, and it does not describe the window end; read the ttm_end dates above, not that label. Flagged to the controller.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.7 on the DCF and 0.3 on peer EV/Sales. The DCF captures NVDA-specific economics (FCF margins of about 42-46% grounded in history, guided gross margin) that EV/Sales ignores. The peer set is small (three) and its multiples rest on much lower-margin earnings bases: TTM P/E is about 122x for AMD, 145x for AVGO and 85x for MRVL, so applying peer EV/Sales to NVDA revenue mixes margin structures that do not match. We keep a 30% weight on peers so the target reflects how the market currently prices AI-semiconductor revenue; the DCF terminal value is about 71% of EV, below 80%, so the DCF is not dominated by the terminal value.
rationales.net_cash: Code computes net cash as mapped cash + short_term_investments - total_debt = 22.443B (F-65cf7ca5f8) + 0 (short_term_investments unmapped; gen-mapping re-verified in round 2 that no snapshot XBRL concept or sum of concepts carries these balances at 2026-07-26) - 33.366B (F-de060525b4, total debt = short-term 1.000B + long-term 32.366B) = -10.923B. The 2026-07-26 balance sheet in the 10-Q text shows two more liquid lines (narrative Q-11 to Q-18). Our judgment on each: (a) Marketable debt securities of $34.143B (Q-11): $33.003B US Treasury (Q-15) and $1.140B US government agency debt (Q-16). These are near-cash, and the company itself reports cash, cash equivalents and marketable debt securities of $56.586B (Q-13, Q-14). They belong in net cash at full value. (b) Marketable equity securities of $42.783B (Q-12): publicly held equities, non-operating and price-volatile; $36.9B of publicly held equity investments are under short-term lock-up restrictions on sale (Q-17), and a further $5.0B long-term locked portion sits in Other assets (Q-18) and is not counted here. We would include them with a 30% haircut, i.e. $29.948B. The haircut combines (1) a marketability discount for the lock-ups, which cover most of the line and prevent monetization at the reported fair value in the near term; (2) concentration and price volatility in AI-related positions; and (3) tax leakage on realization, since a large part of the carrying value is unrealized gains (H1 FY2027 gains from equity securities of $23.7B in the cash flow statement, of which $12.5B were unrealized gains on public equities still held). 30% is an analyst judgment, not a sourced figure. (c) Non-marketable equity securities ($51.157B) stay out: illiquid, carried at cost adjusted for observable prices. Debt is complete (no commercial paper outstanding). Our preferred net cash is therefore -10.923 + 34.143 + 29.948 = +53.168B, against code's -10.923B. Code cannot read this: valuation.value() computes net_cash = cash + sti - debt only from mapped XBRL lines, and there is no input for an override. The published valuation therefore still uses -10.923B. Offline effect with the final inputs here (WACC 10.7%, code's own dcf() and blending formula, 24,285M diluted shares, $209.66 close): code as published: blended $181.53, target $182, upside -13.2%, Underperform. (i) With debt securities only (net cash +23.220B): blended $182.94, target $183, upside -12.7%, Underperform. (ii) With debt securities plus equity at a 30% haircut (net cash +53.168B): blended $184.17, target $184, upside -12.2%, Underperform. For reference, with both lines at full value (+66.003B): target $185, upside -11.8%. Each $1B of net cash adds about $0.041 per share to both legs. The rating does not change in any case, but the code target understates our preferred figure by about $2 per share. We did not change any other input to compensate.
